title: fix(runtime): standalone database-URL refusals name the scheme, never the URL
body:
Fixes #23764
Clause-②: no

## What changed

The standalone host (`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`) now names only the URL's **scheme** in its database-URL refusals and never prints the URL. A password, a username or a query-string token in `OS_DATABASE_URL` no longer reaches the console, the boot log or the `--json` error field.

- `detectDriverFromUrl`'s unsupported-scheme refusal (the card) now reads `Unsupported database URL scheme "redis://"`. Its supported-scheme list is unchanged. The wording follows the CLI host's refusal in PR #23761 (#23633).
- Two sibling refusals in the same file echoed the URL too. Both can carry a credential by measurement (table below), so both are changed here, as the dispatch ruled:
  - the retired in-memory engine refusal (`refuseRetiredMemoryEngine`);
  - the sqlite non-path refusal (`sqliteFilenameFromUrl`).
- One helper, `urlSchemeOf`, extracts the scheme. It uses the same regex the unsupported-scheme arm already tested. A scheme is letters, digits and `+ - .` up to `://`, so it cannot hold a userinfo, a host, a path or a query.

Not changed:
- which URLs resolve, and to which driver;
- the URL handed to the driver, which keeps its credentials;
- where each refusal is raised, and its error class (plain `Error`).

Not touched: `packages/cli`, `createStandaloneStack`'s `mkdirSync` (#23737 remains its own card), and every driver package.

**Why the scheme alone, not a redacted URL.** `packages/runtime` already depends on `@objectstack/spec`, which exports `redactUrlCredentials`. That helper keeps the username, and it strips only the query keys on its credential list. The pin requires that neither the username nor an unlisted token appear. The scheme cannot carry either one, and it is what the operator needs in order to fix the URL.

## Before and after, measured at the public doors

Built CLI and runtime at `c61b1366e1`, with a plain `defineStack` config and `OS_DATABASE_URL=redis://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:6399/0?authToken=PLACEHOLDER-TOKEN`. "Before" is the same build with `standalone-stack.ts` reset to the base `ec44cf60bf` and the runtime rebuilt; it was restored afterwards (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty) and the runtime rebuilt again. The counts are occurrences in the door's whole stdout and stderr.

| door | exit | before: USER / SECRET / TOKEN | after: USER / SECRET / TOKEN |
|---|---|---|---|
| `os dev --no-watch` | 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `os start` | 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `os serve` | 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `os migrate plan` | 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `os migrate recorded-by --json` (stdout `error` field) | 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

- Before: `✗ [StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme: redis://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:6399/0?authToken=PLACEHOLDER-TOKEN. Supported schemes: …`
- After: `✗ [StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme "redis://". Supported schemes: …`

URL to message, per refusal (unit reading at the base, then at HEAD):

| URL (placeholder credentials) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `redis://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…?authToken=PLACEHOLDER-TOKEN` | `Unsupported database URL scheme: redis://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…` | `Unsupported database URL scheme "redis://"` |
| `https://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…` (not a Turso host) | the whole URL | `Unsupported database URL scheme "https://"` |
| `memory://PLACEHOLDER-USER:…` as `databaseUrl` | `The database URL "memory://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…"` | `A database URL with the "memory://" scheme` |
| `memory://PLACEHOLDER-USER:…` as `OS_DATABASE_URL` | `OS_DATABASE_URL "memory://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…"` | `An OS_DATABASE_URL with the "memory://" scheme` |
| a declared default datasource whose url is `memory://…` | `(driver: memory, URL "memory://…")` | `(driver: memory, URL scheme "memory://")` |
| `postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:…` with `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite` | `…does not look like a file path: "postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…"` | `…does not look like a file path (its scheme is "postgres://")` |
| `file:` | `…does not look like a file path: "file:"` | `…does not look like a file path (it names no file after "file:")` |

## Sibling messages in `standalone-stack.ts`

| site | can it carry a credential? (measured) | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `detectDriverFromUrl` unsupported-scheme refusal | yes, any `scheme://user:password@…?token=…` | fixed (the card) |
| `refuseRetiredMemoryEngine`: explicit, env and declared-datasource phrases | yes: `memory://` and `mingo://` accept anything after `//`; all three phrases echoed it | fixed |
| `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` non-path refusal | yes: `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite` beside a credentialed `postgres://` URL echoed it | fixed |
| `unsupportedDriverMessage` (the `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER` value) | not a URL by contract; it carries one only if an operator writes a URL into the driver variable | listed, not changed |
| `assertUrlNamedForRemoteDriver` | names the driver kind only | no |
| the legacy-file notice (`console.warn`) | a state-directory file path, never a URL | no |
| the unreachable-kind `throw` | the kind only | no |

## Mechanism readings

- **(a) Is there a second copy of the URL?** No. Before the change, each door printed each placeholder exactly once: the refusal line. The CLI's `Database:` row already redacts (`redis://127.0.0.1:6399/0`). The error has no `cause`, no door printed a stack, and no file written under `OS_HOME` or the project carried a placeholder. After the change, every door counts 0. The pins also serialise every own property of the thrown error (message and stack) and find no placeholder.
- **(b) Which doors reach it?** All five measured: `os dev`, `os start`, `os serve`, `os migrate plan` and `os migrate recorded-by --json`. A door-level pin would live in `packages/cli`. `packages/cli/test/migrate-exit-code.e2e.test.ts` already drives `os migrate recorded-by --json` over `wat://nope` and reads `Unsupported database URL scheme` from the payload, and that text is kept. This PR does not edit `packages/cli`, by the dispatch's ruling, so the door rows above are a one-time measurement, not a pin.

## Pins

- `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-url-refusal-credentials.test.ts` (new, 30 cases):
  - each refusal, through each door it has (the `databaseUrl` option, `OS_DATABASE_URL`, a declared default datasource, `databaseDriver` / `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER`), driven with `PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@…?authToken=PLACEHOLDER-TOKEN`;
  - each asserts that the refusal still happens as a plain `Error` with no `cause`, names the scheme and the remedy, and that no own property of the error carries any placeholder;
  - CONTROL: 16 rows keep every detection arm (`postgres://`, `postgresql://`, `pg://`, `mysql://`, `mysql2://`, `mongodb://`, `mongodb+srv://`, `libsql://`, `https://*.turso.*`, `wasm-sqlite://`, `*.wasm.db`, `file:`, `sqlite://`, a bare path, a scheme-less relative path, `:memory:`) on the same driver kind, and 3 rows show that a credentialed `postgres://` / `mysql://` / `mongodb://` URL still resolves with `url` byte-identical.
- `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.test.ts`:
  - the `memory://` boot pin now expects `"memory://" scheme` and no URL tail (it used to pin the whole URL);
  - one new boot row: `createStandaloneStack` over a credentialed `redis://` URL rejects, naming the scheme, with no placeholder anywhere on the error.

## Ablation

Run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode), with a shell `trap` that restores from `HEAD` and checks the blob hash. The suites import `./standalone-stack.js` from `src`, so no `dist/` leg applies.

| mutation | red | green |
|---|---|---|
| the raw URL put back into the unsupported-scheme refusal, scheme wording kept | 5: the 4 unsupported-scheme rows and the boot row, all on the placeholder assertion | 116, including every memory, sqlite and CONTROL row and the libsql and mysql suites |
| the raw URL put back into the env memory phrase, wording kept | 1: that row, on the placeholder assertion | 63 |
| the raw URL put back into the sqlite non-path refusal | 2: both sqlite rows, on the placeholder assertion | 62 |

- Every leg reported the anchor going from 1 to 0, a changed blob, and a restore with the blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- The first memory attempt inserted the URL between `scheme` and `selects`. That went red on the wording assertion, not the credential one, so it proved nothing. It was redone with the wording kept (the row above).

## Verification at `c61b1366e1`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` (project `local`): 399 files, 5979 passed, 19 skipped, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` (build program plus test layer): exit 0. The test-layer ledger holds at 27 files / 190 errors. `tsc --listFiles -p tsconfig.test.json` includes both changed test files.
- Changed and neighbouring suites by path: `standalone-stack-url-refusal-credentials`, `standalone-stack`, `standalone-stack.libsql`, `standalone-stack.mysql` and `resolve-project-database`: 155 passed, exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 62 commands, all run, 62 exit 0.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, packages without `dist/`). It was re-run after those were built, and exited 0.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: 62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, all with recorded exit codes.
- Lint, narrowed to the three changed `.ts` files with `eslint --no-inline-config`: exit 0. Three pieces of evidence that the narrowing is sound:
  1. These are the derived change set's lintable files.
  2. `--print-config` shows only per-file syntactic rules and no typed-lint `parserOptions.project`, so no other file can change these files' verdict.
  3. Positive control: a `max-len` of 40 injected on the command line fires on all three files, so none is ignored.
  - The full `pnpm lint` runs in CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- Not run locally, and left to CI: `test:repo` (no repo-project test is changed), the `packages/cli` suites (not touched), and the full lint farm.

## Acceptance notes

- **The CLI host's own `memory://` refusal echoes the whole URL.** It is in `packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts`, the `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` memory arm, which builds `OS_DATABASE_URL "…"` from the raw value. Measured: `OS_MODE=off OS_DATABASE_URL=memory://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:6399/0?authToken=PLACEHOLDER-TOKEN os serve` exits 1 and prints each placeholder once. This is outside this card's file surface and is reported to the seat to file.
- **The sqlite file path strips `file:` case-sensitively, but detection is case-insensitive.** Measured: `OS_DATABASE_URL=FILE:./urd.db os serve` created a directory literally named `FILE:.` in the working directory, with a SQLite file inside it. This is a different defect class from this card's, so it is not changed here and is reported to the seat to file.
- The `resolve-project-database.ts` docstring for `retiredMemoryEngineMessage` still gives `The database URL "memory://"` as an example selection phrase. It is a comment, outside this card's file surface, and left as it is.
